svg.title: How to read the result: two yes-or-no questions give four honest outcomes
svg.desc: A plain how-to-read-the-result guide. The study asks two separate yes-or-no questions. Question one: can a simple straight-line rule read the signed left-minus-right number out of the frozen model, and does it clear the fair baseline of what raw joint coordinates already give? Question two: when the body is mirrored left-to-right, does the number flip to the same size with the opposite sign? Crossing the two answers gives four outcomes. Clean flip means the signed axis is present and behaves like a true mirror. Reads but does not flip means the number is there but the model does not store it as a clean mirror. Does not read is an informative null that explains the weak recorded asymmetry score. Only the side-blind control fires means the signal was an artifact and the signed claim is withdrawn. All numbers are illustrative and transductive; folder labels are dataset annotations, not diagnoses.
svg.text: How to read the result: two questions, four honest outcomes
Two separate yes-or-no checks. Crossing them gives four boxes, each with its own honest claim.
Asymmetry is the weakest scalar (R² ≈ 0.154), so the two right-hand outcomes are the more likely, and both are publishable.
Pull the signed number out AND reach 80% of the raw baseline.
Mirror the body: the number comes back same size, opposite sign.
